{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=causal+tracing+strategies+for+identifying+unrecognized+reasoning+limitations+and+blind+spots+in+LLMs&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7438399\", \"title\": [\"Evaluating Theory-of-Mind Reasoning in LLMs with Temporal Causal Belief Graphs\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Higher-order theory of mind (ToM), the ability to attribute mental states to others, including their beliefs about others' beliefs, remains a persistent challenge in large language model reasoning. We introduce a benchmark of 1,000 multi-agent stories that probes higher-order theory of mind with temporal causal belief graphs. Beliefs propagate between agents node-to-node on a temporal multilayer graph. Edges can be cooperative, deceptive, trusted, or untrusted. To evaluate belief attribution, we use four metrics over the predicted graph versus the ground truth agent beliefs: final node accuracy, time-respecting node accuracy, temporal edge F1, and normalized structural distance. We also measure common knowledge errors and a reality bias, where LLMs default to the true world state even when an agent's belief diverges from it. This paper contributes a benchmark and an evaluation framework for higher-order theory-of-mind reasoning.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7438399\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1108/sd-10-2016-0142\", \"title\": [\"Missing links in effective emerging markets strategies\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:sec>\\n<jats:title content-type=\\\"abstract-subheading\\\">Purpose</jats:title>\\n<jats:p>This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies.</jats:p>\\n</jats:sec>\\n<jats:sec>\\n<jats:title content-type=\\\"abstract-subheading\\\">Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>\\n<jats:p>This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context.</jats:p>\\n</jats:sec>\\n<jats:sec>\\n<jats:title content-type=\\\"abstract-subheading\\\">Findings</jats:title>\\n<jats:p>Clayton Christenson in <jats:italic>The Innovator’s Dilemma</jats:italic> (1997) teaches us that many firms thin…
